_comment: Twelve clusters. A cluster = one pillar page + its spokes, and it exists only if it has a money page to point at. `money_pages` are the /tools/* URLs the cluster is built to feed; `pillar` is the slug of the post every spoke links up to.

clusters.name: YouTube SEO & metadata
clusters.why: The catalog is 23 YouTube tools deep - by far the strongest topical claim the site can make. Every YouTube query we win also lifts the tool pages beneath it.

clusters.name: YouTube monetization
clusters.why: Highest commercial intent on the site and four calculators sitting behind it. People searching payout numbers convert to a calculator run on the first visit.

clusters.name: Image sizes & safe zones
clusters.why: The single largest evergreen query family in the creator space, refreshed rather than rewritten every year, and it maps onto the resizer, the safe-zone guide and every per-platform cropper.

clusters.name: Engagement rate & benchmarks
clusters.why: One tool serves six platforms, so one cluster can rank for six query sets. Benchmarks earn links, which is how a young domain gets authority at all.

clusters.name: Hashtags & discovery
clusters.why: Perennial, per-platform, and the questions are factual (how many, where, which) - exactly the shape we can answer better than a listicle farm.

clusters.name: Instagram formats & profile
clusters.why: Eight tools cover the format problems - carousels, Reels covers, story safe zones, bio previews - which are the queries with an obvious tool answer.

clusters.name: TikTok payouts & formatting
clusters.why: Thin tool coverage but very high query volume; the money calculator and the safe-zone guide carry it until the premium TikTok tools ship.

clusters.name: X & Threads posting
clusters.why: Character limits, thread splitting and link cards are precise technical questions with precise tool answers - the cheapest kind of ranking to defend.

clusters.name: LinkedIn, Facebook & link previews
clusters.why: Lower volume, far lower competition, and the audience has budget. The link-preview debugger serves all three networks from one page.

clusters.name: Pinterest SEO
clusters.why: Pinterest is a search engine, so its users already think in keywords - and four dedicated tools mean we can answer with a checker rather than an opinion.

clusters.name: Writing, scripts & planning
clusters.why: Middle-of-funnel glue: it links every platform cluster together and gives the utility tools (counters, timers, converters) a reason to be linked from prose.

clusters.name: Handles, links & housekeeping
clusters.why: Low-competition utility queries with immediate tool payoff, and the UTM builder pulls in the marketer audience that shares and links.

clusters.name: Short links, redirects & embeds
clusters.why: Five tools land here at once - two shorteners, the expander, the embed generator and the link preview debugger - and the queries are platform-agnostic, evergreen and unusually literal ('shorten youtube link', 'expand short url'). Nobody searching them is browsing: they have a link in the clipboard and a job to finish.

clusters.name: Post mock-ups & screenshots
clusters.why: Six generators now share one workspace, and the query family ('fake instagram post', 'fake tweet') is enormous and almost entirely served by ad-choked single-page sites. The differentiator is not the drawing - it is being the result that tells the reader plainly what these images may and may not be used for.

clusters.name: Saving images from social platforms
clusters.why: Nine downloader tools now sit behind one intent - somebody wants a picture off a platform that would rather they did not have it. The queries are per-platform, high-volume and evergreen, and each one lands on a page that answers it in a single paste.
